intent.goal: Let one verify.py invocation reach two authorities — evidence paths bounded under one root, SHA/git legs run against another — and close round 2's Required findings without widening that change: the legacy no-flag path keeps its 20s symbol-grep budget (S2-R3), the root classifier and the canonical bound are pinned by tests that a mutant cannot walk past (R2-T1/T2/T3), and the fail-closed branch is covered rather than waived (H-7).
intent.ruled_out: A named _LEGACY_GREP_TIMEOUT constant for the restored budget: verify.py's interface WIDTH is a ratchet with two slots left before the pre-deepening baseline, and a timeout is not an interface. The value is passed at the call site and pinned by a test that reads it off the subprocess call and compares it to _run's own default, so it cannot drift back to _git's 10s unnoticed. Also ruled out: waiving the pragma at verify.py:209 — a branch nobody executes is a branch nobody knows the sign of, and the floor guard is right to say so. Also ruled out in this repair: changing verify.py to make the two surviving mutants die. X1 (equal roots forced split) and X3 (artifact bytes read at local HEAD) are ADEQUACY gaps — untouched production already behaves correctly in both, as the new tests assert against it — so a production edit here would be a fourth round, not the authorized repair.
